A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAMBO, with matching authors, core methods, and original benchmarks. The main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 report original optimization experiments on Levy, Schwefel, molecular conformers, drug screening, and stellarator design.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix E adds original runtime measurements, ablations, baseline comparisons, regression evaluations, and regime diagnostics.

M1.justification: The stated EI calculation changes from K components in v1 Eq. (11) to K+1, including the new-regime component, in v2 Eq. (13). This is a limited acquisition-formula revision; implementation changes are not established. The spatial weighting rule, collapsed sampler, and concentration schedule otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix E.4 adds standalone regression on Piecewise-Smooth, Heteroscedastic, and Multi-Scale synthetic targets, plus Diabetes and Energy datasets. This substantially extends task and data coverage beyond the retained seven BO benchmarks. The corrected 80D stellarator label matches the degrees of freedom already specified in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Previously cited but unevaluated Vanilla BO with dimension-dependent length-scale priors (Hvarfner et al., 2024) becomes a comparator across all seven BO benchmarks in Table 3. Table 4 additionally evaluates a finite MoE-GP against DPMM-GP and SGP. Figure 1's original comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include five-fold cross-validated regression RMSE with 300 synthetic training samples, fixed-alpha controls, and single-CPU fitting-only timing measurements. These substantially expand the evaluation protocol. Newly specified Adam and posterior-sampling settings document existing BO experiments rather than establishing changed settings.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds quantitative fixed-versus-adaptive alpha comparisons, computational-overhead analysis, regression tests isolating surrogate quality from acquisition design, and per-regime hyperparameter diagnostics on Schwefel-10D and molecular conformers. These provide substantial analyses beyond v1's optimization curves and qualitative explanations.

E5.justification: Table 4 introduces five-fold cross-validation for estimating regression error, with accompanying ± values whose SE/SD meaning is unspecified. BO results retain mean and standard error over five independent seeds; no increase in BO run counts is established.

E6.justification: Original Figure 1 curves and main-text performance values remain unchanged. Tables 1–6 add extensive results, including fitting times of 32.269 seconds for RAMBO versus 0.542 for TuRBO, and Energy RMSE of 0.957 for DPMM-GP versus 1.436 for SGP. These are newly reported evidence, not demonstrated improvements between versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and new Appendix A distinguish the exact CRP-weighted predictive from the spatially modulated predictive, adding a separate proposition and derivations. Section 3.1 corrects the inverse-gamma conjugacy claim, while Theorem 2.3 and Appendix F refine cluster-count asymptotics and the scheduling proof. These materially revise the mathematical justification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: automatic regime discovery, collapsed inference, adaptive concentration scheduling, mixture acquisition functions, and improved optimization on heterogeneous scientific objectives. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies spatial weighting as a predictive modeling choice and discusses its justification for separated regimes. Appendix E adds interpretations concerning surrogate quality, divergent regime hyperparameters, scheduling stability, and the tradeoff between substantial MCMC overhead and expensive objectives. This substantially expands the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly specifies Adam learning rate 0.05, 200 gradient steps without early stopping, five post-burn-in posterior samples, and pruning threshold 0.001. Algorithm 2 clarifies posterior-sample averaging, and Appendix E reports fitting times. These improve documentation without establishing changed implementation settings; the code link remains the same.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds targeted positioning against Gadd et al. (2020) and Li and Ma (2023), distinguishing predictive weighting and sequential BO from related mixture regression methods. References also add Jeffreys, Tresp's Bayesian committee machine, and Liu et al. (2025). The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the predictive-distribution explanation, related work, and shortened conclusion. v2 adds disclosure, acknowledgements, and impact statements, updates author information, and reorganizes appendix lettering. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, with revised headers and typography. All four existing figures retain their graphical content but are resized and repositioned. Appendix E adds six tables, substantially expanding the visual presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through the exact-versus-modulated predictive distinction, the conjugacy correction, implementation details, and additional empirical controls. The gain is limited by new reporting problems: Tables 2–3 label negative optimization scores as lower-is-better despite the maximization convention evident in Figure 1, and Appendix E.1 claims total wall-clock savings using fitting-only measurements. These inconsistencies weaken the added interpretations without eliminating the benefits of clearer documentation and broader evidence.
